frontier.hypothesis: Making the two tail scratch values non-block-local would stop local_alloc from taking $v0 and remove pseudo 78's hard conflict with hard reg 2 - the last mechanically-unexplored input.
frontier.mechanism: local_alloc runs before global_alloc and only claims pseudos whose live range is inside one basic block (local-alloc.c:472 gates on reg_basic_block[i] >= 0). If the a0+3 value and the 0x8000 constant were live across a block boundary they would fall to global.c instead, and pseudo 78 (priority 30000, allocated first) would face no hard conflict with reg 2.
frontier.next_probe: Recorded for completeness, NOT as a live hope: even with the conflict gone, pseudo 78 carries hard-reg preferences [4,5] and global.c find_reg tries preferred regs first, so it still lands on $a0; and hoisting a0+3 out of the tail re-folds it with s3 (s2/s3 measured this) while hoisting the 0x8000 constant lengthens a live range across calls. Before spending a session on it, measure whether removing the conflict alone changes anything on a throwaway body, and read where the [4,5] preference is actually recorded (global.c set_preference / expand_preferences) rather than assuming.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual is reachable at all from pure C.
